A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, central theorems, and retained experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original norm-distribution simulations, numerical bound comparisons, and CNN and MLP quantization experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds Tiny ImageNet experiments, cross-layer equalization measurements, and MLP experiments with tanh activations.

M1.justification: The principal bound constructions remain unchanged. Section 5.2 adds a simplified AdaRound procedure that learns per-parameter sigmoid offsets using output reconstruction error and regularization, extending v1's fixed floor and nearest-rounding procedures.

E1.justification: v2 adds Tiny ImageNet classification with 200 classes, substantially broadening evaluation beyond the two ten-class datasets in v1. MNIST and CIFAR-10 remain in Appendix E; ImageNet pretraining was already present.

E2.justification: v2 Figure 4 adds simplified AdaRound alongside floor and nearest-rounding quantization and the full-precision reference. Gonon et al. (2023) remains the numerical bound comparator, and the retained MNIST/CIFAR-10 comparisons keep their original comparator membership.

E3.justification: The added Tiny ImageNet evaluation introduces 224-by-224 inputs, 200-output classifiers, 80-epoch SGD fine-tuning, and layerwise calibration using 256 samples and 15 optimization steps. Appendix I also introduces a controlled ReLU-to-tanh substitution. Appendix F's settings for retained experiments are newly disclosed, without establishing that those experiments changed or were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendices H and I add focused analyses of whether cross-layer equalization tightens the norm-based bound and whether depth-dependent trends persist with tanh activations. Existing norm-distribution simulations and depth/bit-width analyses are retained, including material moved to Appendix G.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bars for the experimental results. The added experiments do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds Tiny ImageNet accuracy curves, CLE measurements, and tanh-MLP results. Figure 4 shows over 30% accuracy for four-bit ResNet18 with simplified AdaRound versus below 10% with floor/round quantization; Figure 11 reports r_conv decreasing from 6.01 to 4.66 after CLE. Table 1 and the retained experimental plots are unchanged; these additions are not same-setting gains over v1.

T1.justification: v2 removes the sigma(0) = 0 requirement from Lemma A.2, explicitly adds it to Lemma A.3, and revises the latter's proof to use that assumption. The main approximation bounds and residual-block derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introductory contributions retain the same central claims: tighter approximation bounds, relaxed layerwise norm constraints, and numerical validation on CNNs. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining the principal contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explains how BatchNorm Lipschitz factors would loosen the bounds, interprets CLE as reducing their pessimism, and discusses obstacles to extending the framework to vision transformers. The conclusion replaces the optimization-path research direction with this extension discussion. The existing limitation that bounds greatly exceed observed errors remains.

D1.justification: Appendices D, F, and J substantially expand preprocessing, fine-tuning, frozen-layer, calibration, and hardware documentation, including settings for retained MNIST/CIFAR-10 experiments. However, v1 Appendix D's three-epoch scratch-training recipe for the retained bound-versus-error plots is omitted from v2.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and connections to AdaRound, CLE, AIMET, vision transformers, and attention smoothness, plus MNIST/CIFAR-10 citations. Its central positioning relative to Gonon et al. (2023, 2024) remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 moves the MNIST/CIFAR-10 discussion and simulated norm examples to Appendices E and G, revises the conclusion, removes the Impact Statement, and makes local language edits. Most introductory exposition, section ordering, and proof narrative are retained.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive figure resizing and repositioning. v1 Figures 4–5 and 7–8 become paired panels in v2 Figures 3 and 5; other retained plots move to appendices, and new experimental figures are added. The new Figures 5 and 12 captions incorrectly describe the plotted previous-bound/new-bound ratio in reverse.

improvement.justification: The harder Tiny ImageNet evaluation, targeted supplementary analyses, expanded implementation documentation, and clarified activation assumptions strengthen empirical support and transparency. These gains are tempered by the omitted training recipe for retained bound plots and new ratio-caption errors. The central bounds and their substantial practical looseness remain unchanged, making the overall improvement limited.
